Hello,

I am writing about referral REF-4417. I live in British Columbia. On the phone the desk used the member token member-bc-4417, and I wrote that down before I hung up. The callback number I left is 604-555-0131. Please use that number if a person has to reach me. I am sending this to the Vancouver desk because that is the office that took the call.

I phoned in the small hours of Saturday, 9 January 2027. It was just after midnight in Vancouver. The person on the phone told me Cedar Ridge was booked tonight. I am putting the sentence down as I remember it: booked at Cedar Ridge tonight. I asked them to say the night again. They repeated the same sentence. They did not give me a clock time, a street address, or the name of anyone who would meet me. They said a handset message would follow on the phone I had called from. No handset message arrived.

I kept that phone with me through Saturday. I checked it when I woke, again on Saturday evening, on Sunday morning, on Sunday evening, and once more before I sat down to write this on Monday. The thread that should have held a Northline message is empty. There is no text that names REF-4417. There is no text that names Cedar Ridge. There is no missed call from the desk number I dialled. I looked in the filtered folder as well, in case the message had been pushed aside, and that folder does not have it either. I left the phone on overnight on Saturday because the word tonight sounded as if I was supposed to be somewhere while it was still dark. I am still not sure which night that word was pointing at. It may have meant the night of the call itself, the few hours after midnight on the 9th. It may have meant the coming night of Saturday 9 January, after a normal day. It may have meant tonight as in Monday 11 January, the day I am writing. Those are three different nights. I was given one word, and then silence.

After the call I looked up the clinic, because I had not been a patient at Cedar Ridge and I needed to know where "booked" was asking me to go. What I found is a clinic in Washington. I am in British Columbia. I do not have a trip arranged into Washington this week, and nobody on the phone said the clinic was across the border. I asked, on that same call, whether Cedar Ridge was the Washington clinic. The person did not answer the place. They said the booking sentence again. I am confused about the place, and I am frustrated that the place and the night are both still unclear after a weekend of waiting by the phone. I am not swearing at the desk and I am not accusing anyone of hanging up on me. I am saying the call gave me a clinic name, the word tonight, and a promise of a handset message, and the message did not come.

I am not asking the desk to invent a visit I did not request. I am asking you to reconcile what was said on the phone with what reached the handset. If the visit is for one particular night, I need that night in writing, in a form I can keep, and I need the handset message that was promised. If the Washington clinic is the site on REF-4417, I need a person to say that plainly, and to say what a member who lives in British Columbia is expected to do about a clinic in Washington. If the phone call was about some other place that shares the name, I need that correction with the reference on it. I have only the one name from the call.

Please also check the token against the reference. The person on the phone said REF-4417 and member-bc-4417. If those two strings are not the same case, tell me which one belongs to me, and send the handset message for that one. I do not want a second referral opened because I wrote in. I want the one I already called about to be described in a message that actually arrives.

I rearranged Monday morning around this. I did not go in at my usual time, because I thought a message might still name a time for today and I did not want to be on a bus if it did. It is now 09:40 in Vancouver and the handset message has not come. I will keep this email address open today. Please reply here even if the handset is the path the desk normally uses. I have already seen that the handset path can stay quiet from Saturday midnight through Monday morning.

Thank you for reading the reference, the time of the call, the sentence I was told, and the fact that no handset message arrived. I would like a reply that deals with those points.
